entities.name: The Flood Tablet (Gilgamesh Tablet XI)
entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary: A cuneiform tablet (K.3375) from the Library of Nineveh, now in the British Museum, containing the Mesopotamian flood narrative as told in Tablet XI of the Standard Babylonian Epic of Gilgamesh. Deciphered by George Smith in 1872, its publication caused a sensation in Victorian England because of its striking parallels to the Genesis flood account — including a divine warning, construction of a vessel, loading of animals, a great flood, the sending of birds (dove, swallow, raven), and a post-flood sacrifice. This single tablet revolutionized the relationship between biblical and ancient Near Eastern studies.
